name: template-context
body:
The execution context of a template is not only its field values and rendered body: every slide layout and every section template is also given a reserved data context — a `deck` entry with the deck-wide data (`title`, `author`, `date` and the author's `properties`), a `slide` entry with the current slide's derived metadata (the string position label `number` and the integer `total`), and an `item` entry describing the current instance's place among its siblings (`index`, `number`, `count`, `first`, `last`, `section`, `template`, `parent`; see item-context). At slide level `item` is nil or absent. This is data carried alongside the field values, not a helper: no function is added and the v1 helper set stays exactly `media` (template-language). `deck`, `slide` and `item` are reserved top-level names, unavailable as field or section names in a template (requirements.constraint.reserved-template-names, domain.constraint.template-context-reserved). The same context is present in a slide's layout and in every section instance's execution, at every composition depth.
AC: `{{.deck.title}}`, `{{.deck.author}}`, `{{.deck.date}}`, `{{index .deck.properties "audience"}}` and `{{.slide.number}}` (the string position label) / `{{.slide.total}}` (the integer total) render from a slide layout and from a section template; the `{{.item.*}}` descriptor renders at every depth and is nil/absent in a slide layout; loading a template that declares a field or section named `deck`, `slide` or `item` is a templates error.
